messages.author: 5a37f1244321fb07
messages.subject: RE: qplot - new objects are plotted with the same data
parts:
Dear Gordon,

It happens if you use “vector” instead of “data frame” in the call.

Since I can’t reproduce exactly the same plot since the whole dataset is not posted, but I think you can do:

 

a697 <- qplot(data=subset(raw.table, Name=="697"),  x=Pos, y=Concentration, color=condo, main="697", ylab="Concentration", xlab="Location")

Then a697 will produce the same plot even after you create the next plot.

Let me know if it works..

Kaori

 

 

From: ggp...@googlegroups.com [mailto:ggp...@googlegroups.com] On Behalf Of Lavinia Gordon
Sent: Tuesday, April 23, 2013 7:50 PM
To: ggp...@googlegroups.com
Subject: qplot - new objects are plotted with the same data

 

Hi, can anyone explain to me what is happening here:

My data:
> head(raw.table)
  Include Color Pos Name    Cp Concentration Standard Status cond
1    TRUE   255  A1  697 15.77         1.090        0     NA    A
2    TRUE   255  A2  697 16.01         0.936        0     NA    A
3    TRUE   255  A3  697 16.09         0.894        0     NA    A
4    TRUE   255  A4  697 16.00         0.939        0     NA    A
5    TRUE   255  A5  REH 15.98         0.953        0     NA    A
6    TRUE   255  A6  REH 16.20         0.836        0     NA    A


i <- "697"
# the gene name that I am interested in
mydat <- raw.table[raw.table$Name==i,]
# pulling this genes data out of my table
xvar <- mydat[,3]
yvar <- mydat[,6]
column <- mydat$cond
# checking to see what xvar contains
xvar
[1] A1  A2  A3  A4  P9  P10 P11 P12
384 Levels: A1 < A2 < A3 < A4 < A5 < A6 < A7 < A8 < A9 < A10 < A11 < A12 < A13 < A14 < A15 < A16 < A17 < A18 < A19 < A20 < A21 < A22 < A23 < A24 < B1 < B2 < ... < P24
a697 <- qplot(xvar, yvar, color=column, main=i, ylab="Concentrationa", xlab="Locationa")
a697
# all good!

i <- "REH"
mydat <- raw.table[raw.table$Name==i,]
xvar <- mydat[,3]
yvar <- mydat[,6]
column <- mydat$cond
xvar
[1] A5  A6  A7  A8  P13 P14 P15 P16
384 Levels: A1 < A2 < A3 < A4 < A5 < A6 < A7 < A8 < A9 < A10 < A11 < A12 < A13 < A14 < A15 < A16 < A17 < A18 < A19 < A20 < A21 < A22 < A23 < A24 < B1 < B2 < ... < P24
aREH <- qplot(xvar, yvar, color=column, main=i, ylab="Concentrationb", xlab="Locationb")
aREH
# all good!

Now if I go back and type
a697
the plot for a697 is produced, the header looks good, the xlabs and ylabs are good, but the data plotted is the data from aREH!
It is as if the latest version of the xvar and yvar variables have somehow been used by a697 for plotting.  Can anyone help?!
with thanks for your time,

Lavinia Gordon.
